sources.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite asset sheet for Nova Swarm, a premium top-down arcade space shooter. Create ONE transparent PNG sheet containing exactly TWELVE wholly different enemy spacecraft, laid out in a precise 4-column x 3-row grid, each centered inside its own equal square cell with a wide empty transparent gutter, no overlap. Orthographic top-down view, every ship points its weapons toward TOP of image, same camera and studio lighting. These are final game sprites, not a labeled concept diagram. Remarkably beautiful detailed miniature spacecraft: layered sculpted metal armor, recessed copper machinery, gun barrels, hard surface precision, deep carved dark cavities, tiny contained luminous reactors, elegant directional highlights. Cohesive navy titanium / pearl silver / oxidized copper materials with restrained teal, amber or violet accents. Crucially each of the twelve must have an entirely different unmistakable silhouette and construction, not variants of one fighter: 1 razor-thin twin-boom interceptor, 2 compact armored crab with articulated side claws, 3 wide crescent electromagnetic gunship, 4 angular delta missile bomber, 5 ringless segmented insect craft with a tapered long abdomen, 6 asymmetric salvage tug with two offset engines, 7 triangular three-engine drone carrier with central launch trench, 8 broad hammerhead artillery with two huge cannons, 9 spined crystalline lance with violet internal core, 10 horseshoe siege craft with exposed central furnace, 11 small swept-wing needle scout, 12 hexagonal armored bastion with four diagonal arms. Broad readable shapes first, fine believable machinery second. No circles surrounding craft, no glow halos, no drop shadows, no engine flames, no stars, no backdrop, no lettering, no numbers, no borders, no logos. Real transparent alpha background throughout gaps and gutters. Each entire ship stays inside its own cell and occupies about 75 percent of that cell. Clean alpha silhouettes, no detached debris. High resolution, crisp richly dimensional AAA sci-fi art, not flat vector, not toy-like block models. This is original art not based on any franchise.

Use case: stylized-concept. ONE production sprite sheet for Nova Swarm, twelve original alien enemy spacecraft in an exact 4 columns by 3 rows grid, REAL TRANSPARENT ALPHA background and generous empty gutters. Whole craft fully contained in each cell. Every ship orthographic TOP DOWN, nose at TOP. Photoreal miniature hard-surface sci-fi render quality with rich dimensional lighting, machined metal, layered armor, inset machinery, sharp large silhouettes, crisp details; NOT simple polygon toys or flat vector art. Each is an entirely different architecture: 1 silver manta-ray with four swept narrow fins and orange reactor, 2 emerald industrial lobster with two forward siege claws, 3 violet elongated trident with narrow central spear, 4 ochre rectangular salvage barge with exposed asymmetrical crane, 5 six-wing obsidian moth with a red central eye and no ring, 6 cobalt boomerang interceptor with two massive rear nacelles, 7 white skeletal tuning-fork ship with open central gap, 8 red armored beetle with short broad claw-like wings and dark central carapace, 9 bronze stacked turbine hauler with two side cargo racks, 10 black and jade star-shaped five-prong crystal machine, 11 silver disk-shaped ship with a deep squared bite cut from the front and two cannons, 12 pearl angular swordfish with side-mounted ivory missile pods. All belong to a coherent navy-titanium, aged copper and ceramic-metal universe, with different restrained hull enamels and tiny contained reactor colors. Readable layered engineered construction, sparse brightly colored active weapon apertures. No surrounding circular HUDs, no halos or glow fog, no flame trails, no ground shadows, no text, no symbols, no numbers, no debris, no stars, no scenery, no logos. Exactly twelve ships, all pointing UP, none cropped. Transparent means real alpha, not a painted checkerboard. Final in-game art, original designs not any existing franchise.
